headline: AUDIT DAY: Panama Publishes Final Cobre Panama Report — Restart Decision Imminent for Shuttered Copper Giant
snippet: Panama released its final independent third-party audit of First Quantum Minerals' shuttered Cobre Panama mine today, with President Mulino set to decide the operation's future once the government reviews the findings. The mine produced 350,000 tonnes of copper annually before its 2023 closure and contributed ~5% of Panama's GDP — its fate matters to global copper supply.

headline: WHITE GOLD Corp Fires Up Its Biggest-Ever Yukon Drill Campaign: 35M Tonnes at 1.53 g/t Gold in Play
snippet: White Gold Corp (TSX-V: WGO) launched its largest-ever diamond drilling program across its 305,102-hectare Yukon land package today, targeting expansion of four near-surface gold deposits and testing new regional targets 95 km south of Dawson City. The current indicated resource stands at 35.2 million tonnes averaging 1.53 g/t gold (1.73 Moz) with a further 32.2 million tonnes inferred.

headline: GOLD $4,501 / SILVER $75.87: US-Iran 60-Day Ceasefire Extension Calms Inflation Fears, Metals Stabilize
snippet: Gold held near $4,501 and silver rose to $75.87 on Friday after Washington and Tehran agreed to extend their ceasefire 60 days, begin nuclear program talks, and discuss unrestricted Strait of Hormuz shipping — ending the energy-price inflation fears that had knocked gold to a two-month low below $4,400 mid-week. Both metals remain up 35%+ year-over-year.

headline: CENTRAL BANKS Added Net 20 Tonnes of Gold in May — Record 43% Now Plan to Increase Holdings
snippet: World Gold Council data shows global central banks purchased a net 20 tonnes of gold in May — slightly below the 12-month average of 27 tonnes but part of an accelerating structural trend: 95% of central bankers now expect official reserves to grow, and a record 43% plan to actively increase gold holdings over the next 12 months.

headline: CHINA WON'T BUDGE: Rare Earth Controls Unchanged After Trump-Xi Summit — Yttrium Exports to US Down 95%
snippet: Despite Beijing summit language about 'addressing US concerns on critical minerals,' China's April 2025 rare earth export regime remains fully intact with no timeline, verification mechanism, or definition of 'address' agreed. CSIS research shows US yttrium imports collapsed from 333 metric tons to just 17 tons in the eight months after controls took effect.

headline: AUSTRALIA BOOTS Six China-Linked Investors From Rare Earth Miner Northern Minerals — Deadline Sunday
snippet: Australia's Treasurer ordered six China-linked entities holding ~27% of Northern Minerals (ASX: NTU) to divest within 14 days, with the deadline falling this Sunday (May 31). The forced divestment protects the Browns Range dysprosium-terbium project — which, once operational, would be the first significant non-Chinese source of processed dysprosium globally.

headline: SIXTH STRAIGHT YEAR: Silver Supply Deficit Hits 46M oz — Cumulative Draw Since 2021 Now Nears 762M oz
snippet: The Silver Institute's World Silver Survey 2026 projects a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of ~46 million ounces, with cumulative draws since 2021 approaching 762 million oz — yet near-term price direction is caught between Iran deal optimism, sticky 3.8% CPI data, and oil-price risk. J.P. Morgan's full-year target is $81/oz; Citigroup targets $110 for H2.

headline: STILL $5,000+: Why Goldman, JPMorgan, and Wells Fargo Haven't Abandoned Their 2026 Gold Forecasts
snippet: Despite gold's retreat to ~$4,501 from its $5,600 Q1 peak, major banks hold year-end targets of $5,000–$6,300: Goldman Sachs ($5,400), Societe Generale ($6,000), Wells Fargo ($6,100–$6,300), JPMorgan ($5,000+ with $6,300 possible). The structural case rests on central bank demand, de-dollarization, and a 41% YoY price gain that analysts interpret as regime change, not a peak.

headline: NEWMONT vs. SSR Mining: Which Gold Producer Actually Wins When Gold Is Stuck at $4,500?
snippet: Motley Fool analysts compare the world's largest gold producer — Newmont, which generated $7.3B in free cash flow in FY2025 — against cash-rich intermediate SSR Mining, which is debt-free, trading at cheaper forward multiples, and poised to collect $1.5B from the sale of its troubled Turkish Copler mine. Analyst edge: SSR on valuation, Newmont on scale and diversification.

headline: AMNESTY WARNING: U.S. Lithium Mining Boom Across Nevada Is Violating Indigenous Peoples' Rights
snippet: Amnesty International's May 2026 report finds the rush to develop over 100 proposed Nevada lithium projects — driven by EV battery demand — is systematically bypassing Indigenous Peoples' rights to free, prior, and informed consent. The finding adds a growing ESG and legal risk dimension to domestic lithium projects at a time when U.S. policy is aggressively pushing for supply-chain independence.
